'''Charles Lee Wilkins''' (August 14, 1938 – June 27, 2025) was an American chemist who is a distinguished professor of chemistry and biochemistry at the [[University of Arkansas]] and the founding director of the University of Arkansas Statewide Mass Spectrometry Facility.<ref name="Profile">{{cite web |title=Charles Wilkins Distinguished Professor, Analytical Chemistry |url=https://cell.uark.edu/profile.php?uId=cwilkins |website=University of Arkansas |access-date=9 April 2021}}</ref>

==Background==
Wilkins was born in [[California]] on August 14, 1938.<ref name="SCALACS">{{cite web |title=1993 Charles L. Wilkins, UC Riverside |url=https://scalacs.org/?page_id=1141 |website=Southern California Section of the American Chemical Society |access-date=9 April 2021}}</ref> He earned a Bachelor of Science degree from [[Chapman College]] and a PhD from the [[University of Oregon]].{{Citation needed|date=July 2022}}

Wilkins died after a short illness in [[Fayetteville, Arkansas]], on June 27, 2025, at the age of 86.<ref>{{cite web |title=Charles Lee "Charlie" Wilkins |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/name/charles-wilkins-obituary?id=58858052 |website=Legacy |access-date=18 July 2025}}</ref>

==Career==
Wilkins was a distinguished professor of chemistry at the [[University of California, Riverside]] and a chemistry professor at the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]].<ref name="Profile" /> In 1993, Wilkins was a recipient of the [[Tolman Award]].<ref name="SCALACS" />

With [[Michael L. Gross (chemist)|Michael Gross]], he built the second Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometer and they were the first to use it for analytical applications.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Gross |first=Michael L |author2=E.B. Ledford Jr |author3=R.L. White |author4=S. Ghaderi |author5=C.L. Wilkins |year=1980 |title=Coupling of Capillary Gas Chromatography and Fourier Transform Mass Spectrometer |journal=Analytical Chemistry |volume=52 |issue=14 |pages=2450–2451 |doi=10.1021/ac50064a056}}</ref><ref name="Analytical">{{cite web |title=Charles Wilkins |url=https://theanalyticalscientist.com/powerlist/2019/charles-wilkins |access-date=9 April 2021 |website=The Power List 2019 – 21-100 (A-Z) |publisher=The Analytical Scientist}}</ref> In November 2020, Wilkins was selected as the chief editor of the ''International Journal of Analytical Chemistry.''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wilkins Selected as Chief Editor of International Journal of Analytical Chemistry |url=https://news.uark.edu/articles/55187 |access-date=2022-07-09 |website=University of Arkansas News |language=en}}</ref>
